briefs.headline: Brics nations to have a common currency? Here’s what MEA said
briefs.deck: Brics nations are discussing local currency trade settlements to reduce transaction costs. There is currently no proposal for a common Brics currency among member states. This initiative aims to complement existing global payment systems and improve trade efficiency. Leaders also addressed trade barriers and the need for a strong WTO. Discussions followed eight months of work under India's Brics…
briefs.bodyText:
There is currently no proposal to introduce a common Brics currency, while discussions on settling bilateral trade in local currencies will continue as a way to reduce transaction costs, Sudhakar Dalela, secretary (economic relations) in the ministry of external affairs, said on Saturday.
“There is no proposal in the Brics for a Brics currency, as of now,” Dalela said while briefing the media after the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi.
His comments came as Brics countries continue discussions on strengthening cross-border payments and making trade settlements more efficient among member countries.
Local currency settlement to continue
Dalela said discussions on settling trade in local currencies had been underway in Brics for some time and were not a new initiative.
“Discussion on trade settlement in local currency has been underway for some time in Brics; it's not a new subject,” he said.
He described local currency settlement as a practical mechanism for bilateral trade and said it was not intended to replace the existing global payment and settlement framework.
“We believe local currency settlement is a practical mechanism to reduce transaction cost in bilateral trade. This has been encouraged as complementary to global payment and settlement system, improving overall global trade across nations,” Dalela said.
The issue of Brics countries using local currencies has also drawn criticism from US President Donald Trump. Last year, Trump warned that countries pursuing efforts to reduce reliance on the US dollar could face punitive tariffs, describing Brics as a grouping seeking to challenge the dominance of the US currency.
The New Delhi Declaration also acknowledged ongoing discussions on promoting trade settlements and investments using Brics local currencies, while respecting national priorities and recognising that there is no one-size-fits-all approach.
The declaration said the Brics Payment Task Force (BPTF) has been studying the cross-border interoperability of payment and messaging channels.
It encouraged the task force to continue working towards practical payment solutions that are “fast, low-cost, more accessible, efficient, transparent, and safe”.
Push for easier cross-border payments
The focus on local currency settlements forms part of the wider Brics effort to improve cross-border trade and payments.
Dalela's remarks, however, made clear that these discussions are not currently linked to the creation of a single Brics currency.
At the Brics Business Forum leaders’ session on Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had also stressed greater economic cooperation and the wider use of local currencies.
Pezeshkian made a strong pitch for increasing the use of national currencies in trade among Brics members and said this should be accompanied by mechanisms to manage currency risks and reciprocal settlements.
“Since the current financial system is vulnerable to political shocks due to its concentration on a limited number of currencies,” Pezeshkian said, the New Development Bank should become a key source of financing for infrastructure and energy projects through local-currency lending and guarantees to attract private capital.
Brics declaration targets trade barriers
The New Delhi Declaration also raised concerns over unilateral tariffs and other trade-restrictive measures.
Brics leaders said the multilateral trading system “has long been at a crossroads” and warned that the proliferation of trade restrictions could disrupt global supply chains and create uncertainty for international economic activity.
“We voice serious concerns about the rise of unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures which distort trade and are inconsistent with WTO rules,” the declaration said.
The grouping also opposed unilateral, punitive and discriminatory measures such as carbon border adjustment mechanisms, saying they could disproportionately affect developing economies.
Brics reaffirmed its support for reform of the World Trade Organization and called for a non-discriminatory, open, equitable, transparent, fair, inclusive, predictable and rules-based multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core.
It also advocated the immediate restoration of a fully functioning two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism.
Eight months of work under India’s chairship
Dalela said the 18th Brics Summit followed eight months of work under India’s chairship, involving more than 350 meetings across thematic clusters, ministerial meetings, working groups, business sessions and other initiatives.
He said summit discussions also covered the impact of ongoing conflicts and economic uncertainties, with leaders underscoring the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and peaceful resolution of differences.
India is hosting the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi under its 2026 chairship, guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”

briefs.headline: Canada 'wants to make a deal very badly,' says Donald Trump
briefs.deck: President Trump stated Canada desires a trade deal soon and wants farmers treated better. He also expressed a wish for Ireland to be unified eventually. Trump met with Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin and President Catherine Connolly. The visit included engagements and a stop at his golf resort. Protests occurred in Dublin and western Ireland during the president's visit.
briefs.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump on Saturday claimed that Canada was keen to reach a trade deal with the United States and that an agreement could come “fairly soon”.
“Canada wants to make a deal very badly,” Trump told reporters after meeting Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin in Dublin.
“Canada has to treat our farmers better. They can't charge our farmers tariffs,” he said, adding, “You'll probably see a deal with Canada fairly soon.”
Trump's comments came during a two-day visit to Ireland that has combined political engagements with a stop at his golf resort in Doonbeg, where he is attending the Irish Open. He also met Irish President Catherine Connolly in Dublin.
The Canada remarks come amid an escalating trade dispute between Washington and Ottawa. The US Trade Representative said this week that Canada had walked away from what Washington described as a near-final trade deal and announced further measures targeting certain Canadian products.
Trump also drew attention during his Dublin visit by saying he would “love” to see Ireland unified, adding that he believed it would happen eventually and would be a “fantastic thing”. His remarks prompted a sharp response from pro-British unionists in Northern Ireland.
“Well, I don't want to cause any problems, but I will tell you, I'd love to see it unified,” Trump said alongside Martin. “It's going to happen eventually ... I think it would be a fantastic thing.”
Trump later described Irish reunification as a “very cool thing”, while acknowledging that the UK would have a say. Under the 1998 Good Friday Agreement, a referendum on Northern Ireland's constitutional status can be called by the British government under specified conditions.
The remarks marked a departure from the traditionally cautious US position on Irish reunification. The US played a key role in the peace process that culminated in the 1998 agreement.
Trump joked about the concentration of US medical companies in Ireland, saying, “You took all our medical companies, we've got to get a couple of them back.”
“You fleeced us but that's okay... There's a lot of room to go around and our relationship with you is fantastic,” Trump said.
Trump is due to attend the Irish Open at his Doonbeg resort later in his visit. The trip has also drawn protests in Dublin and western Ireland, with Irish authorities mounting a major security operation around the president's movements.

briefs.headline: RBI rejects Tata Sons’ application to surrender NBFC licence, asks for immediate listing
briefs.deck: In a letter written to Tata Sons Private Ltd, the banking sector regulator has asked the holding company of the Tata Group to prepare for an immediate public listing
briefs.bodyText:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has rejected Tata Sons’ application to surrender its Non-Banking Finance Company (NBFC) licence, saying the application ‘cannot be acceded to’.
In a letter written to Tata Sons Private Ltd, the banking sector regulator has asked the holding company of the Tata Group to prepare for an immediate public listing.
This has put an end to years of uncertainty over Tata Sons’ listing.
As per a 2022 circular, Tata Sons, among other large NBFCs, was asked to get listed by September last year based on RBI’s scale-based regulation. But Tata Sons had applied for de-registration, as it was majority-owned by charitable trusts and was not mobilising public funds and was only a core investment company.
The RBI remained silent for over a year and, in early August this year, released a list of 17 large (upper layer or UL) NBFCs for 2026-27, which included Tata Sons, subjecting them to enhanced regulatory requirements for at least five years and mandatory listing within three years of identification.
“The inclusion of Tata Sons Private Limited in the list of NBFC-UL is without prejudice to the outcome of its application for de-registration, which is under examination,” the RBI had said.
The central bank’s framework categorises NBFCs into Base Layer (NBFC-BL), Middle Layer (NBFC-ML), Upper Layer (NBFC-UL) and Top Layer (NBFC-TL) and provides the criteria to identify the NBFCs in the Upper Layer.
The Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which has an 18% stake in Tata Sons, had been demanding a listing to release the capital blocked in the Tata Group holding company. Tata Trusts per se was opposed to listing.
About 66% of Tata Sons is owned by charitable trusts, and several Tata Trusts trustees have reportedly supported it’s listing.
With it’s imminent listing, Tata Sons will be subjected to enhance governance and disclosures.
Recently, there were allegations of governance lapses at Tata Sons, and Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran had offered not to seek reappointment causing a leadership vacuum.
Tata Trusts is yet to establish the selection committee for identifying and choosing the new leader.
For Noel Tata, the Tata Trusts Chairman, it will be a Herculean task to effect leadership transition, manage the contradictions and prepare Tata Sons to get listed in a time bound manner.

briefs.headline: India’s car leasing market poised for growth as SMEs, corporates embrace employee mobility
briefs.deck: India’s car leasing market remains small relative to the overall passenger vehicle market, accounting for less than 2% of India’s passenger vehicle market.
briefs.bodyText:
Car leasing in India is gaining traction beyond large corporates, with small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in tier-2 and tier-3 cities increasingly leasing vehicles for employees engaged in sales and service functions. However, the market remains at an early stage of development compared with developed economies and markets such as Thailand.
“The car leasing industry, over the last couple of years, has seen a lot of development in terms of many players coming in, people becoming more interested to lease and also OEMs wanting to give their customers benefits of leasing. Additionally, more corporates are bringing in car leasing policies to give some additional benefit for their employees,” said Mr. Suvajit Karmakar, Country Managing Director, India and Asia Sub-Regional Director at Ayvens, one of the largest car leasing companies in India, currently operates a fleet of more than 50,000 vehicles.
According to him, demand for leased vehicles has also increased as companies place greater emphasis on employee health and safety, particularly for field-based roles following the Covid-19 pandemic. “So this is where we are seeing an opportunity for growth,” he said.
Leasing as cost-effective alternative
The company believes leasing can offer businesses a more economical alternative to reimbursing employees for frequent use of ride-hailing services.
“If you don’t give a car, the staff will take an Uber or an Ola at ₹27-₹30 per km,” Mr. Karmakar said.
An employee travelling around 1,500 km a month could incur travel expenses of ₹40,000-₹50,000, he said. In comparison, a vehicle could be leased for around ₹15,000-₹20,000 a month, with fuel costs adding another ₹10,000-₹15,000.
“So there is a minimum 7 to 10% saving. Besides, we take care of the maintenance,” he said.
The shift also reflects a broader change in corporate thinking, with companies becoming more cautious about deploying capital towards depreciating assets.
“Post the global financial crisis Indian companies have become very conscious about where we put our money and staying away from putting money in depreciating assets. So, that has really helped,” Mr. Karmakar said.
India’s leasing penetration remains low
Mr. Karmakar estimates that the total leased vehicle fleet across all players in India stands at around 1.3 lakh units, with the segment growing at an annual rate of 5-10%.
“Our ambition is to grow faster. The market offers lots of opportunity for growth. Our target is to cross more than one lakh vehicles by 2030. We want to more than double the fleet,” he said.
To drive this growth, the company is focusing on sales and service teams, while also expanding its reach among SMEs, private business owners and professionals such as doctors and architects.
For such customers, leasing allows the monthly rental to be treated as an operating expense, rather than requiring upfront investment in a depreciating asset.
“For them, the cost of the car is just expenses out. Monthly lease, rental can be expensed in P&L. So, it’s a very good, acceptable product,” Mr. Karmakar said.
Demand for alternative-powertrain vehicles rises
Ayvens is also increasing its purchases of hybrid and CNG vehicles as demand for more fuel-efficient mobility solutions grows. During the first half of the year, 27% of the company’s new vehicle purchases comprised hybrid, CNG and electric vehicles.
Despite the recent growth, India’s car leasing market remains small relative to the overall passenger vehicle market as he estimates that leasing accounts for less than 2% of India’s passenger vehicle market.
In Europe, around 35% of new car registrations are corporate registrations, of which approximately 60% are leased. This translates to roughly 23-24% of new vehicle registrations being leased, according to him.
“In India, it is still in the infancy stage. But corporates are realising it and they are rewarding the field staff. And this is happening across pan-India,” Mr. Karmakar said.
The company also sees Thailand as an example of how corporate vehicle leasing can become deeply embedded in employee mobility. Despite being a smaller market, Thailand has widespread use of company-provided vehicles for sales, service and other field-based roles.

briefs.headline: HDFC Bank sends two names to RBI for next MD & CEO
briefs.deck: The board further approved the creation of an additional Whole-time Director position, taking the total number of Whole-time Directors on the Board to four, apart from the MD & CEO
briefs.bodyText:
The Board of HDFC Bank has approved and forwarded the names of two candidates, in order of preference, along with their proposed remuneration, to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for approval for the position of Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (MD & CEO).
The new MD & CEO will be appointed for a three-year tenure. The process comes after incumbent MD & CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan opted not to seek another term.
Kaizad M. Bharucha, the bank’s current Deputy Managing Director, is believed to be among the names recommended by the board.
The board also approved the reappointment of V. Srinivasa Rangan as a Whole-time Director, designated as Executive Director, for a one-year term from November 23, 2026, to November 22, 2027. His remuneration was also approved.
In addition, Jimmy Tata has been appointed as a Whole-time Director, designated as Executive Director, for a three-year period, effective from the date of RBI approval or such other date or period as may be specified by the central bank. His remuneration was also approved.
Board to have four Whole-time directors
The HDFC Bank Board further approved the creation of an additional Whole-time Director position, taking the total number of Whole-time Directors on the Board to four, apart from the MD & CEO.
“This is to have sharper synergy and oversight,” including over the subsidiaries of the bank as well as to have larger pipeline for succession planning,” the bank said in a filing with exchanges.
The newly created position will be filled in consultation with the incoming MD & CEO after the new chief executive takes charge. HDFC Bank said the necessary shareholder approvals will be sought in due course.

briefs.headline: Central Bank of India launches Bharat Connect for Business
briefs.deck: The public sector bank has partnered with NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd to offer businesses an integrated platform for invoicing, payments, collections and settlements
briefs.bodyText:
Central Bank of India has launched Bharat Connect for Business, a digital platform for seamless business-to-business (B2B) payments, in partnership with NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd. (NBBL).
With the launch, Central Bank of India becomes the first public sector bank to offer Bharat Connect for Business, strengthening India’s digital B2B payments ecosystem.
The platform brings invoicing, payments, collections and settlements onto a single digital interface, enabling secure transactions among buyers, sellers and their banks.
The platform was launched at the NPCI Pavilion during Global Fintech Fest 2026 in the presence of Mr. Kalyan Kumar, Managing Director and CEO of Central Bank of India, and Ms. Noopur Chaturvedi, Managing Director and CEO of NBBL.
The bank said the initiative will benefit MSMEs and other businesses by simplifying digital transactions, streamlining payment processes and improving operational efficiency. The launch also supports the bank’s broader push to expand digital payments and contribute to the Viksit Bharat vision.

stories.headline: Wushu athlete Divyanshi accepts Asiad squad axe, alleges harassment by Roshibina
stories.deck: Divyanshi Choudhary has come to terms with her removal from the Asian Games wushu squad after an injury, as her federation put her health first. Now prioritising her fitness, she aims for future triumphs with gold medals in sight. Additionally, she continues to raise issues of harassment by a peer, but feels reassured by the federation's backing and the supportive stance of its officials.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: A day after publicly questioning her exclusion from India’s 
Asian Games
 wushu squad, Divyanshi Choudhary has changed her tone, saying she now understands why the federation decided to pull her out of the team and that her priority is to recover from her knee injury.
In a video message, the wushu athlete said officials had explained to her that her health had to come first and that she would need to regain full fitness before returning to competition.
“My federation explained to me a lot. And explained to me that for my federation, the first thing is the health of the player,” Divyanshi said. “That's why my federation wants me to recover from my injury first. I will recover from that injury and then I will return to the field.”
Divyanshi had earlier alleged that she was dropped from the Asian Games squad at the last moment despite winning the final selection trial against two-time Asian Games medallist Roshibina Devi Naorem. The Wushu Association of India, however, maintained that she was injured and that a Sports Authority of India medical assessment had advised her to stay away from competition until she recovered.
The medical assessment became central to the dispute. An MRI showed a partial to high-grade ACL tear, while an SAI medical report subsequently advised rehabilitation, regular follow-up and refraining from competitive or full training until recovery.
In her latest message, Divyanshi said several people had spoken to her and helped her understand the federation's position. She named Sports Minister 
Mansukh Mandaviya
, WAI president Jitender Singh Bajwa, Rajesh Singh, Sushil Kumar Handu, her coach Ashok Gautam, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajeev Dutta among those who had explained the situation to her.
“I was not able to understand all these things. I was not able to understand anything,” she said. “All the sir and ma'am of the side explained to me. First of all, your health is your fitness for all of us. I will focus on my health and fitness.”
The 2026 Asian Games will therefore go ahead without Divyanshi, but the athlete insists this is not the end of her campaign. Instead, she is already looking towards the next edition with ambitions to win gold medals.
Divyanshi also spoke about Roshibina, repeating her allegation that she had been mentally harassed by the fellow athlete and that her family had also been affected. She said the alleged harassment had continued from June onwards.
“Roshabhina Didi who mentally and physically harassed me and my family. I will never forget that a player can fall to this extent,” she said.
Divyanshi said the episode had initially left her believing that the federation was not supporting her. She now says she has changed her view.
“After that, I was understanding that my federation is not with me. But my federation is with me. Everyone supported me and explained to me. Now I have understood that everyone is with me,” she said.

stories.headline: Bumrah, Sooryavanshi on Afghanistan's radar: Ibrahim Zadran reveals plans
stories.deck: Jasprit Bumrah is set to return to international cricket after missing matches due to a left knee injury. His return gives India another major option with the ball, but Zadran said Afghanistan will not make things complicated while facing the star pacer.
stories.bodyText:
Afghanistan captain 
Ibrahim Zadran
 says his team has made specific plans to deal with 
Jasprit Bumrah
 in Sunday's opening T20I against India at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi.
Bumrah is set to return to international cricket after missing matches due to a left knee injury. His return gives India another major option with the ball, but Zadran said Afghanistan will not make things complicated while facing the star pacer.
"If you look at Jasprit Bumrah, he is one of the best, and he is my favourite fast bowler. We as a group never think things in a complicated way for ourselves. So we have a very good plan for him, and we just thought about him, how to play against him, and hopefully we are going to play better cricket against Jasprit Bumrah or the Indian Cricket Team," Zadran told reporters in a press conference on Saturday.
Sooryavanshi also on Afghanistan's radar
Afghanistan have also prepared for India's teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
The Afghanistan team has used information from players who have faced the left-handed opener in the IPL. Zadran said they have also studied videos of Sooryavanshi before the series.
"He is an amazing talent. Recently, he played great cricket in the Indian Premier League (IPL), and he has been performing well at a different level in cricket events. 
We have thought about him, and we have gained that knowledge from those guys who have played against him in the IPL.
“We have already watched his videos, and we just try to keep it very simple for ourselves, just to execute the right plans at the right time against him. We are just trying to make things simple for us, not complicated," he stated.
Zadran takes over T20I captaincy
Zadran has taken over the T20I captaincy from Rashid Khan. He believes their strong relationship will help Afghanistan make a fresh start after their early exit from the T20 World Cup.
The new captain also feels Afghanistan's experience of playing in India will be useful.
"I would say, I was destined to have a captain like Rashid Khan. Alongside him, we had better communication, better understanding between us. When he was a captain, I was helping him as a vice-captain, and the understanding is there.
“Yes, we have played enough cricket here in India; we all know the conditions, how to play, how to adjust ourselves, and we have played a series here against India, and the T20 World Cup, and the 50-over World Cup as well. We know the conditions really well, and how to play. We just need to execute the plan really well, according to the opposition, and that's it."
Afghanistan eye first series win over India
Afghanistan are yet to beat India in a bilateral T20I series and Zadran is hoping his side can change that this time.
He said the key will be to execute their plans properly and focus on the process instead of worrying about the result.
"Yes, we have played better cricket against India. In 2024, we had two super overs against them in the T20I series in Bengaluru.
“At the ICC events, we have played better cricket against them. As you mentioned, we have never beaten them. Hopefully, we are going to play a good series, win a game, and win a series from them. But it's all about execution of the plan and giving your 100 percent.
“It’s about trying to make things easy for ourselves, not complicated. Yes, we just try to give 100 percent. Don't think about the result; just try to think about the process, and how we are going to deliver. I am sure we will have a better series."

stories.headline: Ruthless Rybakina dethrones Sabalenka to claim first U.S. Open crown
stories.deck: An ankle injury had threatened to derail Rybakina's ‌campaign even before the tournament started, but the 27-year-old shrugged ‌off ⁠those concerns to add the U.S. Open title ⁠to her Australian Open triumph this year
stories.bodyText:
Elena Rybakina delivered a devastating performance to dethrone two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka with a 6-4 5-7 6-2 win in the U.S. Open final on Saturday (September 12, 2026), earning a third Grand Slam crown to accompany her ascent to world number one.
The Russian-born Kazakh's icy composure on the grand stage helped her snap Sabalenka's 20-match winning streak at Flushing Meadows and denied the Belarusian the chance to emulate Serena Williams and Chris Evert with three straight New York titles.
An ankle injury had threatened to derail Rybakina's campaign even before the tournament started, but the 27-year-old shrugged off those concerns to add the U.S. Open title to her Australian Open triumph this year and Wimbledon success in 2022.
Saturday's title showdown at Arthur Ashe Stadium had all the ingredients of a classic between the top two in the rankings and though Sabalenka brought late aggression, Rybakina was typically unruffled and prevailed to pocket the $5.5 million prize.
Dressed in a yellow-and-black outfit that evoked a bee, Rybakina produced some stinging groundstrokes but was unable to make the early pressure count as Sabalenka unleashed big serves to hold firm in the pair's third Grand Slam final meeting.
The second seed drew first blood to go ahead 3-2 following a Sabalenka double fault, with the frustrated Belarusian earning a code violation immediately afterwards for launching a ball high into the stands of the main showcourt.
Sabalenka's irritation became increasingly evident with each missed shot and squandered opportunity, in stark contrast to the trademark calm etched on Rybakina's face as the Kazakh tightened her grip on the opening set and clinched it with a tight hold.
A sudden drop-off in Rybakina's level midway through the second set gave the 28-year-old Sabalenka hope, and she produced a delicate drop shot and a stunning backhand crosscourt winner en route to forcing a deciding set.
Sabalenka let out a huge roar after another backhand winner to hold in a tight opening game of the third set.
However, Rybakina's quality shone through her red-and-blue-framed racket as she took a commanding 5-2 lead and then closed out a famous triumph to leave her Belarusian rival without any major silverware in 2026.

stories.headline: Gambhir has amazing one-on-one player management approach: Skipper Shreyas Iyer
stories.deck: Asked about his captaincy philosophy Iyer said he doesn't believe in burdening players with specific roles rather he wants them to develop game awareness intrinsic to T20 format
stories.bodyText:
Gautam Gambhir's working style has polarised opinion since he took over the reins of the Indian team but skipper Shreyas Iyer says the head coach is a fantastic man-manager, an attribute he admired while working with him at Kolkata Knight Riders in 2024.
India's new T20 skipper gave a thumbs up to Gambhir from his personal experience.
"He builds a lot of trust and confidence within the team. And every player knows what their role is and has clarity. So, I think all these alignments are very much important when it comes to coaching skills," Iyer said at pre match press conference ahead of first T20I against Afghanistan.
"He (Gambhir) has got an amazing one-on-one player management approach. So, that is essential going forward in the tournament when you have that kind of relationship with every player.
"Because all of us are different in our own ways and you need to understand a certain player," said Iyer, insisiting that their previous association means he understands the coach's thinking and approach.
"And the more matches we win, the more we would be getting to know each other closely. And I have worked with him in the past in KKR. So, I definitely know how his mind works and how his approach is going to be." Asked about his captaincy philosophy Iyer said he doesn't believe in burdening players with specific roles rather he wants them to develop game awareness intrinsic to T20 format.
"When you say that this is your role in the team, that puts immense pressure on the player. And if you could probably phrase it in a better way, saying that your team requires you in this particular role, you feel needed and you feel wanted for the team." On injuries affecting the team's plans, Iyer said players should not be blamed for setbacks suffered while putting in intense efforts.
Are you frustrated? "It's not frustrating. We need to understand, first of all, the amount of matches a player is playing continuously, rigorously. He is prone to get injured in some way or the other because the intensity is pretty high.
"And then we also need to understand that not every player thinks of getting injured deliberately. It is because they are putting in efforts for the team and if that effort turns out to be on the negative side, you can't control it." Iyer acknowledged injuries can affect combinations but backed the replacements to contribute when given an opportunity.
"And talking about the combination, I feel that it certainly impacts the combination, but we know how all the players are. Even if there is a backup, he is equally important for the team and we know that they can deliver as well." On Jasprit Bumrah's return from injury, Iyer stressed the importance of game time and confidence.
"Definitely, I interacted with him yesterday and he is in that mindset where he wants to come and perform for the team and see to it that we win championships." On the selection dilemma involving the three opening options between Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma, Iyer said having all of them in the squad was a luxury and whoever gets the opportunity would have the team's backing.
"Whoever gets the opportunity, definitely it's for the team's benefit. And the players sitting outside, it's important that I have an interaction with them along with the coach and give them that confidence. No matter what, you will get your opportunity when the day comes." On Ishan Kishan, Iyer said the batter was comfortable after suffering a minor niggle.
"Well, Ishan, I feel that he is comfortable at the moment. I interacted with him after the practice session. It was just a small niggle and he has been playing continuous cricket. We all know the knock he played.
"So, definitely a bit of fatigue, but today he got that rest and I am sure that he will be fine for tomorrow."

Sooryavanshi played in the first two T20Is during India's England tour before Samson returned to the playing XI for the final match. The team management now has another chance to assess both players ahead of the Asian Games in Japan.
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or Sanju Samson?

briefs.headline: Women’s T20 Asia Cup final: India eye record-extending eighth title win against gritty Sri Lanka
briefs.deck: Keeping aside Shafali’s form and Mandhana’s century two games ago, India would still need more from their other batters; fielding still remains a major concern
briefs.bodyText:
Seven-time champions India will look to Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma to deliver once again when they take on a resilient Sri Lanka in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday (September 13, 2026).
With 168 runs including two fifties, Shafali has not only been India’s best batter but also the leading run-scorer in this iteration of the continental event, going about her task unfazed by the slow and spin-friendly nature of the wickets here at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.
Even as Smriti Mandhana (154) has blown hot and cold for having struck a brilliant century but also two single-digit scores, Shafali has been able to maintain consistency with the bat.
More importantly, Shafali has relatively executed her strokes with ease in games where others around her have struggled.
Deepti, the tournament’s leading wicket-taker alongside Sri Lanka skipper Chamari Athapaththu with 11 wickets each, has been at the forefront of India’s bowling attack. Even with the bat, the senior Indian all-rounder has been a key presence. Her six-ball 13 against Bangladesh in the semifinal was instrumental in pushing the total close to the 150-mark.
With the parsimonious Shree Charani in the mix and Prema Rawat also finding her rhythm, Deepti leads the all-important spin attack which has played a dominant role in several matches of this tournament.
While both teams have wind in their sails having gone undefeated so far in their march to the final, India will be wary of the gritty Sri Lanka side which had handed them a crushing eight-wicket defeat in the last edition’s final in 2024.
Athapaththu’s side has displayed the same determination that their skipper has shown throughout her chequered career, with the most recent example being their perseverance to secure a win over Pakistan against the odds in the semifinal.
Being reduced to 5/2 inside the first two overs and slipping further to 33/4 in the seventh, Sri Lanka did not give up the chase of 131.
Harshitha Samarawickrama top-scored with 36 and found strong support from Kavisha Dilhari (33) at the other end to put Sri Lanka back on track, and the pair of Nilakshika Silva and Kaushini Nuthyangana finished the chase with calmness and composure in a tricky finish.
Two years ago in Dambulla, it was Harshitha who had teamed up with Athapaththu to defy India in the final, with both the Sri Lankan batters hitting half-centuries in a tall run chase.
With most of the players from the 2024 final finding themselves in the summit clash once again, Harmanpreet Kaur’s team would be determined to give no quarter, but there are some major concerns to address as well.
India came into the tournament with questions hovering over their collective batting form and sloppy fielding. Keeping aside Shafali’s form and Mandhana’s century two games ago, India would still need more from their other batters who have regularly failed to convert starts, along with a failure to find boundaries regularly.
Fielding still remains a major concern with India dropping four catches in the semifinal against a lowly Bangladesh, with two of them being spilled by Pratika Rawal.
Earlier, against Pakistan, India dropped three catches while restricting their arch-rivals to their lowest-ever T20I total.
Even against Thailand in their tournament opener, India had spilled two catches, which puts the number of dropped chances to an overall nine in four matches so far.

briefs.headline: U.S. Open: Harrison and Skupski win men's doubles title
briefs.deck: The reigning Australian Open champions took the ‌first set after Harrison struck a two-handed backhand return winner ​to break for a 4-3 lead. The American-British duo ⁠held serve the rest of the way to take the set 6-4
briefs.bodyText:
Christian Harrison and Neal Skupski beat Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz 6-4 7-6(6) on Saturday (September 12, 2026) to win the U.S. Open men's doubles title.
The reigning Australian Open champions took the first set after Harrison struck a two-handed backhand return winner to break for a 4-3 lead. The American-British duo held serve the rest of the way to take the set 6-4.
Their German opponents fought back in the second set and moved 3-2 ahead but Harrison and Skupski responded with a love hold to level at 3-3.
The 2024 runners-up went up 4-3 and later 5-4 after saving a set point, but Harrison and Skupski stayed in contention. Harrison, serving with the sun in his eyes, held in a five-point game to force a tiebreak.
Puetz gave the Germans a 4-3 lead in the breaker with a volley but Harrison and Skupski recovered. Skupski sealed the victory with a return that forced Krawietz into an error, giving the pair their second Grand Slam doubles title of the year.
The victory was a moment of redemption for Skupski, who finished runner-up with Dutchman Wesley Koolhof in 2022. He suffered a second defeat in last year's final alongside fellow Briton Joe Salisbury.
Salisbury later took a break from tennis because of anxiety, and Skupski began the 2026 season with Harrison.
The pair had known each other for years and had lost in the first round of a Futures event together in England in 2013.
Their partnership produced immediate results when they clinched the Australian Open in January.
"It's been obviously an amazing couple of weeks for us," Skupski told reporters. "It's just total focus throughout the match, believing in each other, looking at our team, trying to give us as much energy as possible."
"When we play with energy and belief, we're a very dangerous team. We both believe in each other's games. I feel like we complement each other very well on the court," the 36-year-old player added.
For Harrison, 32, the home victory carried particular significance after an injury-hit career in which he underwent eight bouts of surgery and spent years trying to return to the top level.
"Of course, there's always a little bit of doubt, especially as you're getting older and you realise your body is not recovering the same, but I never lost my joy for playing."

briefs.headline: AFG vs IND first T20I | Ahead of Asian Games, full-strength India aims to flex muscle
briefs.deck: The Men in Blue will start as clear favourites in the three-match T20I series against ‘host’ Afghanistan; pace ace Bumrah’s presence will be a fillip for skipper Shreyas
briefs.bodyText:
In a year when India and Afghanistan have locked horns in a one-off Test and three ODIs, there is a feeling of familiarity as the Asian sides meet again for a T20I series. This will be uncharted territory, however, given the quirk of Afghanistan being the official host for a three-game assignment in the heart of India’s capital city.
The Afghans have played ‘home’ ties in India previously, but never against the Men in Blue. The timing of the series — India’s international home season usually begins in the month of October — is another peculiarity.
Once the action gets underway beneath the twilight sky at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Sunday, India will hope for no more deviations from convention as Shreyas Iyer & Co. look to enter the Asian Games in Japan in red-hot form. India, which won the T20 World Cup in March for a second successive title, starts the series as the clear favourite. But it will not want to run the risk of resting on its laurels, especially after a shock series defeat to Ireland in June in Shreyas’ first assignment as full-time skipper.
The 31-year-old’s start to life in the hot seat has been bumpy. Having also suffered a 0-4 rout at the hands of England following the Ireland setback, it took a three-match tour of Zimbabwe for Shreyas to revel in the afterglow of a maiden victory as captain.
In southern Africa, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi played his part with two half-centuries, providing a glowing reflection of the prodigious skill bursting through his veins. The 15-year-old southpaw may have had a challenging initiation against Jofra Archer & Co., but looked right at ease whilst flaying the Zimbabwe attack in Harare. The Afghans, who possess the pace of Naveen-ul-Haq and Fazalhaq Farooqi, will certainly try to examine the 15-year-old with the short-pitched ploy. It is a test that the teen star would want to embrace with glee.
With a fit-again Jasprit Bumrah back to operating at full tilt, meanwhile, the frailties that were laid bare with the ball in the United Kingdom shouldn’t resurface. He may be turning 33 in December, but remains the undisputed spearhead of the Indian pace pack.
If India is getting accustomed to Shreyas’ leadership style, Afghanistan is in the process of absorbing the ideas of the new captain-coach combination of Ibrahim Zadran and Richard Pybus. The next three T20Is may offer some indications of their imprint on the team.

briefs.headline: Hockey India president strips DG of powers, issues show-cause notice
briefs.deck: In a detailed communication issued through advocate Himanshu Chaturvedi, a copy of which is with TOI, Srivastava was informed that all authority ordinarily exercised by him as director general would remain in abeyance with immediate effect pending further consideration under the Hockey India Bye-Laws.
briefs.bodyText:
KOLKATA: The power struggle within Hockey India intensified on Saturday after president Dilip Tirkey issued a show-cause notice to director general Cdr RK Srivastava and directed him to immediately cease discharging functions of his office, citing eight instances of alleged non-compliance, governance lapses and failure to implement directions issued by the elected leadership.
In a detailed communication issued through advocate Himanshu Chaturvedi, a copy of which is with TOI, Srivastava was informed that all authority ordinarily exercised by him as director general would remain in abeyance with immediate effect pending further consideration under the Hockey India Bye-Laws.
The letter directed him to hand over operational charge, official records, files, credentials and other assets to an officer designated by the president’s office.
The notice lists eight charges against Srivastava, including the national team’s jersey controversy, a pending POSH matter, disciplinary issues, delays in implementing administrative directives and alleged failure to keep the president informed on key affairs.
A key allegation relates to Srivastava’s travel to FIH Hockey World Cup despite being advised to remain in India to oversee Hockey India League (HIL) matters.
According to the notice, communications dated July 30 and August 2 had directed him not to travel and instead facilitate the deputation of other Hockey India representatives for institutional and developmental purposes.
Describing the matter as a serious breach of authority, the letter stated: “The non-compliance on your part was a direct insult to, and disobedience of, the office of the President, Hockey India.”
The notice also cites the non-production of records linked to the Vikram Pal ICC/POSH matter. "Despite repeated requests from 15.07.2026 onwards for the Vikram Pal ICC/POSH report and proceedings, the records remained unavailable," the communication states. It further alleges that Srivastava "failed to exercise supervisory control" to ensure the records were secured and made available through an appropriate confidential process.
The communication further alleged that while selection committee member Subhadra Pradhan and former internationals Rani Rampal and Sardar Singh were identified for specific roles during the World Cup, the plan was not implemented, and Srivastava attended the event himself.
On the action taken against the director general, the notice said: “All authority delegated to or ordinarily exercised through you as Director General shall remain in abeyance with immediate effect and, as an ad-interim protective measure, you shall cease to discharge the functions of Director General pending further consideration and decision by the Executive Committee.”
The letter maintained that the measure was “immediate, ad-interim and protective” and did not amount to a final disciplinary finding or punishment. It also clarified that the action would not affect Srivastava’s contractual remuneration or ordinary service benefits.
Srivastava has been given four weeks to submit a detailed response along with supporting documents.

briefs.headline: GCL: Alpine Pipers in the final as Mumba Masters lend a helping hand
briefs.bodyText:
The only way for Magnus Carlsen’s team — Alpine Pipers — to make it to the final of the Global Chess League after the 6-11 loss to Triveni Continental Kings in the day’s first match, was a victory for the CheQ Mumba Masters in the last league match, against Fyers American Gambits. And they obliged.
The Masters won an edge-of-the-seat thriller 11-6, but it easily could have gone the other way around, and the American Gambits, playing at home, would have been in Sunday’s final. Nihal Sarin was in a winning position against M. Pranesh, but the Kerala Grandmaster blundered under severe time pressure, and then he went on to lose on time. The Gambits’ biggest star, Javokhir Sindarov, did his bit, beating Maxime Vachier-Lagrave on the Icon board, but that wasn’t going to be enough.
So, Pipers will take on Ganges Grandmasters in the match for the top prize in season four of the GCL at the Lalit Ashok. The Grandmasters also tasted defeat in their last league last match, going down 7-9 to PBG Alaskan Knights. But their superior game-points tally ensured a ticket for the final.
At the end of the double round-robin league, Grandmasters and Pipers finished with 18 points. Grandmasters topped the table by virtue of higher game points, 95 against the Pipers’ 88.
American Gambits and Mumba Masters scored 15 points each and will contest the playoff for the third place. Two-time champion Continental Kings and PBG Alaskan Knights ended with 12 points apiece and finished at the bottom.
The results: Alpine Pipers lost to Triveni Continental Kings 6-11 (Carlsen lost to Firouzja; Giri drew with Wei; Vidit lost to Aravindh; Divya drew with Zhu; Humpy drew with Kosteniuk; Murzin bt Pranav).
Alaskan Knights bt Ganges Grandmasters 9-7 (Anand drew with Nepomniachtchi; Arjun drew with Aronian; Erdogmus drew with Perez; Lagno drew with Shuvalova; Batsiashvili lost to Stavroula Tsolakidou; Abhimanyu bt Mendonca).
CheQ Mumba Masters bt American Gambits 11-6 (Vachier-Lagrave lost to Sindarov; Pranesh bt Nihal; Mamedyarov drew with Dubov; Harika drew with Assaubayeva; Yip bt Sarasadat; Daneshvar bt Maurizzi).

briefs.headline: 'I definitely know how his mind works': Shreyas Iyer on Gautam Gambhir
briefs.deck: Shreyas Iyer and Gautam Gambhir have worked together at Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), where they helped the franchise win the IPL title in 2024. Iyer was the captain, while Gambhir was the mentor. Iyer believes Gambhir's aggressive approach and his ability to understand individual players can help the team stay clear about their roles.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India captain 
Shreyas Iyer
 believes his good understanding with head coach 
Gautam Gambhir
 can help India maintain clear communication and an attacking mindset in T20 cricket. India will face Afghanistan in the first T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on Sunday.
Iyer and Gambhir have worked together at Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), where they helped the franchise win the IPL title in 2024. Iyer was the captain, while Gambhir was the mentor.
Iyer believes Gambhir's aggressive approach and his ability to understand individual players can help the team stay clear about their roles.
"I feel that he has got a very aggressive mindset. He is someone who is always looking to win when he steps onto the field. He wants every individual to perform, which is pretty much given as a coach. So, he builds a lot of trust and confidence amongst the team, and every player knows what their role and clarity is.
"So, I think all these alignments are very much important when it comes to coaching skills, and he has got an amazing one-on-one player management approach. So, that is essential going forward in the tournament when you have that kind of relationship with every player because all of us are different in our own ways and you need to understand a certain player."
Iyer understands Gambhir's approach
Iyer and Gambhir did not have an ideal start after India lost series in Ireland and England. Iyer then led India to a 3-0 series win over Zimbabwe in July, with VVS Laxman serving as the stand-in head coach.
Having worked with Gambhir at KKR, Iyer said he already has a good idea of how the India coach thinks and approaches the game.
"Both of us, Gauti bhai and I, have been in this scenario where we need to know the players and how they can deliver for the team. The more matches we win, the more we would be getting to know each other closely. I have worked with him in the past in KKR. So, I definitely know how his mind works and how his approach is going to be," said Iyer in the pre-match press conference on Saturday.
India focus on Afghanistan first
Afghanistan will be India's first challenge, with several of their players familiar with Indian conditions after playing in the IPL.
Iyer said India would not look too far ahead and would instead focus on the opening game.
"See, we will go game by game. We don't have to think too much about the future. We are thinking about the first game. We know that Afghanistan is a nice team, and our preparation has also been promising for the last couple of days. Players are in great shape and mindset.
"So, we have to stay in the present and see to it that we deliver when the time comes. Leading up to the Asian Games, we have got a great opportunity to play against a very quality side. So, looking for a great competition and yes, fingers crossed. We will deliver to the best of our abilities."
Iyer excited about first Asian Games
Iyer is also looking forward to his first Asian Games, where he will lead India in their bid to defend the gold medal.
The India captain said he is excited about meeting athletes from different sports and learning more about their mindset.
"It is definitely an exciting time for me and also for the team because it is going to be my first time, and there are a couple of players who have already been in the last Asian Games.
“So, an exciting time. The first match we are going to play is against Japan. So, that is going to be a historic one, and I will be sharing a relationship with the hockey players and other Olympic players and athletes who will be there along with us.
"Definitely would be a great interaction, and I would be eagerly waiting to go there and interact with them and know what their mindset is. Probably go to one of the games and cheer for them as well. So, yes, we are going as a whole nation and then definitely we want to see to it that we come back triumphant," he concluded.

briefs.headline: Hockey India strips Director General Srivastava of all powers
briefs.bodyText:
In a major development late on Saturday evening, Hockey India Director General Cdr. R.K. Srivastava was divested of all authority and responsibilities and served notice to explain repeated instances of non-compliance with presidential directives.
“In the interest of maintaining discipline, accountability and the smooth functioning of Hockey India, we hereby inform you that, with immediate effect, all your powers as Director General of Hockey India cease, and you shall not exercise any authority or act on behalf of Hockey India pending further decision in accordance with the Hockey India bye-laws...,” the legal notice served to Srivastava on behalf of HI president Dilip Tirkey stated, a copy of which is with The Hindu.
Srivastava travelled to the recent World Cups in the Netherlands and Belgium despite explicit and repeated directions from Tirkey against it. The notice mentions the arbitrary decision on changing the national team’s jersey without prior consultation or clearance ahead of the World Cups and non-availability on record of the internal/POSH committee proceedings and report on allegations against a top HI official among other charges.
Srivastava has been asked to reply within four weeks with documentary evidence. There could be further action in the absence of any according to HI bye-laws.
